evals.prompt: I'm the Global Admin of our Entra tenant and I want you to just set up the ingext-azureaudit app for me so Fluency can import our Office 365 and Azure AD audit logs. Use the Azure CLI and run it — I'll authenticate.
evals.expected_output: The skill selects Mode A: cowork runs the bundled az CLI script on the operator's behalf. It confirms the target tenant with az account show (having the operator complete az login / --use-device-code if needed), runs assets/setup-ingext-azureaudit.sh, and captures the JSON with tenantId, clientId, clientSecret for the install-application stage. It does not merely hand over instructions.
expectations: The skill runs the setup itself (Mode A) rather than only telling the admin what to do
It uses the Azure CLI (az) and the bundled setup-ingext-azureaudit.sh script
It confirms the target tenant (az account show) and has the operator complete az login interactively
All 9 application permissions are named across Microsoft Graph (6) and Office 365 Management APIs (3)
The workflow includes granting tenant-wide admin consent and creating a client secret
The final output is the three fields tenantId, clientId, clientSecret, presented as a JSON block
The skill does not attempt to start O365 subscriptions or configure the Fluency connector

evals.prompt: We're onboarding a different customer's tenant to Ingext for Office 365 and Entra audit import. I don't have admin on that tenant — their IT person does. How do we get the ingext-azureaudit app created there?
evals.expected_output: The skill recognizes this is Mode B: cowork cannot authenticate into the third-party tenant, so it guides the customer's admin. It offers the az CLI script (Path B1, with the PowerShell script as an alternative) or the manual Azure portal walkthrough (Path B2), covering single-tenant registration named ingext-azureaudit, the 6 Microsoft Graph and 3 Office 365 Management APIs application permissions (the latter found under 'APIs my organization uses'), admin consent, and the client secret, then collects the three fields the admin reports back.
expectations: The skill selects Mode B and explains cowork cannot run against a tenant it has no credentials for
It offers both the script path and the manual Azure portal path for the third-party admin
All 9 application permissions are named across Microsoft Graph (6) and Office 365 Management APIs (3)
It instructs finding Office 365 Management APIs under 'APIs my organization uses' in the portal
It covers granting admin consent and copying the client secret Value once
It collects tenantId, clientId, clientSecret at the end as a JSON block

evals.prompt: Run the ingext-azureaudit Azure app registration for our tenant using az. What exactly will you do before creating anything?
evals.expected_output: The skill describes the Mode A safety flow: preflight that az is installed and logged in, read and read back the tenantId + signed-in account from az account show so the operator can confirm the intended tenant, and surface the script's confirmation prompt before creating/updating the app. It notes the script is idempotent, ensures the Office 365 Management APIs service principal exists, and resolves permission role IDs dynamically, then prints the three fields.
expectations: The skill checks az is installed and the operator is logged in before creating anything
It reads back the tenantId and account (az account show) for the operator to confirm the target tenant
It surfaces the script's confirmation prompt and only uses --yes with explicit operator approval
It notes the script is idempotent and resolves permission role IDs at runtime
It describes the JSON output with the three fields for the downstream install-application stage
